instruction: How do I stop weevils from destroying my stored maize?
output: Dry the maize well before storage until the grain is hard, about 13% moisture. Shell it, then keep it in clean, airtight containers, metal silos, or hermetic bags to cut off oxygen. A food-grade grain protectant also helps. Clean the store first, keep new grain away from old grain, and inspect monthly, removing any infested grain.

instruction: My cassava leaves have yellow blotches and the roots are rotting with brown streaks. What is it?
output: This looks like cassava brown streak disease, spread by whiteflies and infected cuttings. The roots develop a brown, corky rot that makes them unusable, and there is no cure. Uproot and destroy affected plants, plant only clean cuttings from healthy plants or tolerant varieties from your extension office, and harvest early before the rot spreads.

instruction: What is boring into my maize stems and how do I control it?
output: That is likely stem borer. The larvae tunnel into stems, causing dead-heart and weak stalks that snap. Destroy crop residues after harvest to kill hiding larvae, plant early, and rotate with legumes. A push-pull system using Desmodium between rows and Napier grass around the field repels the borers. In small plots you can split affected stems and remove larvae by hand.

instruction: My maize has pale yellow streaks running along the leaves and the plants are stunted. What should I do?
output: These pale streaks along the veins point to maize streak virus, spread by leafhoppers, and it cannot be cured. Remove and destroy badly affected plants, plant early at the recommended time to avoid peak leafhopper numbers, and control grassy weeds that host the insect. Use tolerant varieties from seed suppliers or your extension office for future crops.

instruction: How do I know if my soil is too acidic for maize?
output: Signs of acidic soil include stunted, yellowing crops, poor response to fertilizer, and strong growth of weeds like sorrel. The sure way is a soil test from your extension office. If the soil is acidic, below about pH 5.5, apply agricultural lime a few months before planting and add organic manure. Liming gradually and adding compost raises the pH over time.

instruction: Can I use animal manure instead of buying fertilizer, and how much?
output: Yes, well-rotted manure improves the soil and feeds crops. Compost it first for 2 to 3 months so it does not burn roots or spread weed seeds. Apply two to four handfuls per planting hole, or spread and mix it into the soil before planting. Manure alone is often low in nutrients, so combine it with a smaller amount of mineral fertilizer for the best yields.

instruction: When is the best time to weed my maize field?
output: Keep maize weed-free for the first 6 weeks, when weeds compete most for water and nutrients. Do a first weeding about 2 to 3 weeks after emergence and a second around 5 to 6 weeks, before tasseling. Weed when the soil is moist so removal is easier, and avoid disturbing the maize roots. Timely early weeding protects yield far more than late weeding.

instruction: How should I space and plant my beans for a good harvest?
output: Plant beans at the onset of steady rains in well-drained soil. Space rows about 40 to 50 cm apart with 10 cm between plants, sowing seeds 3 to 5 cm deep, one to two per hole. Use certified, disease-free seed, weed early, and rotate with cereals like maize to reduce root diseases. Avoid waterlogged spots, as they cause the seeds and roots to rot.

instruction: There is orange powder on my bean leaves that rubs off on my fingers. What is it?
output: That orange powder is bean rust, a fungal disease that spreads in warm, humid weather. Remove and destroy badly affected leaves and avoid working among wet plants to reduce spread. Space plants for good airflow, rotate away from beans for a season, and plant resistant varieties. If it appears early and spreads fast, an approved fungicide can help, following the label and safety directions.

instruction: My tomato leaves are curling and the plants are stunted. What is wrong?
output: Upward leaf curling with stunting is often caused by whitefly-spread viruses. Whiteflies must be controlled early: use yellow sticky traps, remove and destroy infected plants, and keep the field free of weeds that host them. A silver or reflective mulch repels whiteflies. Grow resistant varieties where available, and avoid planting new tomatoes next to old infected ones.

instruction: My tomato fruits have a dark sunken patch at the bottom. What causes this?
output: That is blossom-end rot, caused by uneven water and calcium reaching the fruit, not by an insect or disease. Water regularly and evenly so the soil does not swing between wet and dry, and mulch to hold moisture. Avoid too much nitrogen fertilizer, which worsens it. Adding lime before planting supplies calcium in acidic soils. Remove affected fruits so the plant feeds the healthy ones.

instruction: How can I reduce aflatoxin in my groundnuts?
output: Aflatoxin comes from a mould that grows on damaged or poorly dried nuts. Harvest at the right maturity, avoid injuring the pods, and dry them quickly on racks or clean tarpaulins, not on bare soil. Dry until the kernels are hard and rattle. Sort out shrivelled, discoloured, or mouldy nuts before storage, and keep them in dry, ventilated bags off the floor. Never eat mouldy nuts.

instruction: How do I make good compost from crop and kitchen waste?
output: Build a heap or pit layering dry material like maize stalks and leaves with fresh material like weeds, kitchen scraps, and animal manure. Add a little soil and water each layer so it is moist but not soaked. Turn it every 2 to 3 weeks to add air and speed rotting. It is ready in 2 to 3 months when it is dark, crumbly, and earthy-smelling. Apply it to fields before planting.

instruction: How can I stop soil erosion on my sloping farm?
output: On slopes, plant along the contour rather than up and down. Make contour bunds or dig trenches to slow runoff, and plant grass strips like Napier or vetiver across the slope to trap soil. Keep the ground covered with crops, mulch, or cover crops so rain does not hit bare soil. Trees and hedges along boundaries also hold soil. These measures keep topsoil and water on your field.

instruction: What does NPK on a fertilizer bag mean and which do I need?
output: The three numbers are the percentages of nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and potassium (K). Nitrogen drives leafy green growth, phosphorus helps roots and early establishment, and potassium supports strength and fruit or grain filling. Use a phosphorus-rich fertilizer at planting for good roots, and a nitrogen source like urea for top-dressing. A soil test tells you exactly what your field lacks.

instruction: Aphids are covering my vegetable plants. How do I get rid of them without expensive chemicals?
output: Aphids are small soft insects that cluster on shoots and the underside of leaves, sucking sap. Spray them off with a strong jet of water, or use a homemade soap solution of a little liquid soap in water on the affected parts. Encourage natural enemies like ladybirds by avoiding broad sprays. Remove heavily infested shoots. Check plants often, as early action stops a small problem becoming large.

instruction: How do I choose and prepare good cassava cuttings for planting?
output: Select cuttings from healthy, mature plants 8 to 12 months old, free of leaf mottling or streaks. Use the middle, woody part of the stem, cutting pieces about 20 to 25 cm long with several nodes. Plant soon after cutting, at a slant or flat, with two-thirds in the soil, at the start of the rains. Using clean cuttings from healthy plants is the best way to avoid mosaic and brown streak disease.

instruction: When and how should I transplant my rice seedlings?
output: Transplant rice seedlings when they are about 3 to 4 weeks old and 15 to 20 cm tall, into a well-puddled, levelled field with shallow standing water. Plant two to three seedlings per hill, spacing hills about 20 cm apart in rows. Transplanting young seedlings in rows gives stronger tillering and easier weeding than broadcasting. Keep the field moist and weed early for a better yield.

instruction: How do I plant sweet potato vines for a good root harvest?
output: Use healthy vine cuttings about 30 cm long from disease-free plants, taking the tip and middle sections. Plant on ridges or mounds, burying two to three nodes at a slant, spacing plants about 30 cm apart. Ridges help the roots swell and drain excess water. Weed early, and where weevils are a problem, keep exposed roots covered with soil and rotate fields between seasons.

instruction: Is it safe to apply fertilizer when the soil is dry?
output: Applying fertilizer to dry soil wastes it, because the nutrients cannot dissolve and reach the roots, and nitrogen can be lost. Apply just before or after rain, or when the soil is moist, and work it lightly into the soil rather than leaving it on the surface. Avoid placing fertilizer directly touching seeds or stems, as it can burn them. Keep a few centimetres of gap from the plant.

instruction: My groundnut leaves have small dark spots with yellow halos. What is it?
output: Those spots are groundnut leaf spot, a common fungal disease that can cause leaves to drop and lower yields. Remove and destroy crop residues after harvest, rotate with cereals so the fungus does not build up, and avoid planting groundnuts on the same land year after year. Use certified seed and resistant varieties where available. Severe cases may need an approved fungicide used per the label.

instruction: How can I control weeds without spending money on herbicides?
output: Weed early and often by hand or hoe while weeds are small, especially in the first few weeks after planting. Mulch with crop residues or leaves to smother weeds and hold moisture. Close plant spacing shades the ground and slows weed growth. Rotating crops and using cover crops between seasons also suppresses weeds. Never let weeds set seed, as that multiplies next season's problem.

instruction: How do I know when my maize is ready to harvest?
output: Maize for dry grain is ready when the husks turn brown and dry and the kernels are hard and dented, with a black layer at the kernel base. Test by pressing a kernel with your nail; if it does not dent, it is dry enough. Harvest promptly in dry weather to avoid mould and pest damage in the field, then dry the cobs further before shelling and storing.

instruction: What are cover crops and how do they help my soil?
output: Cover crops are plants grown to protect and improve the soil rather than for harvest, such as lablab, mucuna, or cowpea. They shade the ground to stop erosion and weeds, and legume covers add nitrogen. When dug in or left as mulch, they add organic matter that improves moisture holding and structure. Grow them in the off-season or between rows, then cut and incorporate before they seed.

instruction: Birds are eating my sorghum before harvest. What can I do?
output: Bird damage is worst as the grain ripens. Plant your sorghum at the same time as neighbours so no single field is the only target, and choose varieties with tight heads or a bitter tannin coat that birds avoid. Scare birds actively during grain filling using guards, reflective tape, or noise, especially in early morning and evening. Harvest promptly once mature to cut losses.

instruction: How do I control termites attacking my crops and stored wood?
output: Termites attack weak or stressed plants and dry residues. Keep crops healthy with good spacing, water, and organic matter so they resist attack. Remove old stumps and residues that feed colonies, and locate and destroy the nest where possible. Wood ash or an approved soil treatment around planting holes can help in bad cases. Mulching and manure keep the soil moist, which reduces termite pressure.

instruction: Insects are attacking my cowpea flowers and pods. How do I protect them?
output: Cowpea flowers and pods are attacked by thrips, pod borers, and pod-sucking bugs, which cause flower drop and empty pods. Scout the crop from flowering and act early. Neem-based sprays help against young insects, and removing damaged pods reduces build-up. Time planting so flowering avoids peak pest periods. If using an approved insecticide, spray at flowering per the label and observe safety intervals.

instruction: How can I improve a tired field that gives poor yields every year?
output: Continuous cropping without replenishing nutrients exhausts soil. Rebuild it by adding compost or well-rotted manure, rotating in legumes like beans or cowpea that fix nitrogen, and returning crop residues instead of burning them. Give part of the land a rest or grow a cover crop, and add mineral fertilizer based on a soil test. Combining organic matter and fertilizer restores fertility better than either alone.

instruction: How can I protect my cattle from East Coast Fever?
output: East Coast Fever spreads through the brown ear tick. Control ticks by dipping or spraying cattle with acaricide weekly in the wet season and every two weeks in the dry season, and slash tall pasture. Where available, ask your vet about the ECF infection-and-treatment vaccine. Treat sick animals early with the right drug from a vet; delay is often fatal.

instruction: My dairy cow's milk has dropped. What should I feed her?
output: Milk falls when energy and protein are low. Give plenty of good forage such as Napier grass cut before it flowers, plus a legume like Desmodium or Calliandra for protein, and a little dairy meal at milking. Always keep clean water free-choice; a cow needs 40-60 litres a day. Provide a mineral lick. If the drop is sudden, check for mastitis and worms.

instruction: How often should I deworm my goats?
output: Deworm at the start and end of the rains, when worms peak, and whenever goats look thin, pot-bellied, or have pale gums (a sign of the barber's pole worm). Rotate grazing and avoid wet early-morning grass to cut reinfection. Alternate dewormer types between seasons so worms don't build resistance, and always deworm does before kidding.

instruction: My cow's left side is swollen and tight after grazing. What is wrong?
output: That is bloat, usually from grazing lush, wet legumes. Keep the animal standing and walk it slowly to help it belch. Drench with 250-500 ml of cooking oil to break the froth and massage the left flank. If breathing becomes hard and it worsens fast, call a vet urgently. Prevent bloat by feeding dry roughage before turning cattle onto lush pasture.

instruction: Is zero-grazing better than letting my cattle roam?
output: On a small plot, zero-grazing (cut-and-carry) often works better. You bring fodder to a shed, so you use less land, control ticks and disease more easily, and collect manure and urine for crops. Build a dry, well-ventilated shed with a raised slatted floor. It suits improved dairy breeds, while free grazing suits large open rangeland.

instruction: What is the vaccination schedule to protect my chickens from Newcastle disease?
output: Use the heat-tolerant I-2 Newcastle vaccine as an eye drop. Vaccinate chicks at about 2-3 weeks, repeat at 3-4 weeks, then boost every 3-4 months, ideally before dry-season outbreaks. Vaccinate only healthy birds, keep the vaccine cold in a flask with ice, and use it the same day. Vaccination prevents the disease but cannot cure already-sick birds.

instruction: How do I feed my hens so they lay more eggs?
output: Laying hens need extra protein and calcium. Give a layer ration, or mix grain with a protein source like sunflower or soya cake, and add crushed limestone or dried, crushed eggshell for strong shells. Offer greens and kitchen scraps, and keep clean water always available since egg is mostly water. Provide 14-16 hours of light and control lice and worms, which cut laying.

instruction: How do I keep young chicks alive in their first weeks?
output: Chicks cannot control their body heat, so keep them warm: about 35C in week one, lowering roughly 3C each week until they feather. Watch them: huddling means too cold, spreading to the edges means too hot. Give clean warm water and chick starter or fine mash, keep bedding dry, and protect them from rats, cold drafts, and damp.

instruction: My young chickens are passing bloody droppings. What should I do?
output: Bloody droppings usually mean coccidiosis, common in warm, damp, dirty litter. Treat the whole flock promptly with an anticoccidial such as amprolium in the drinking water for the full course. Keep litter dry and birds not overcrowded, clean waterers daily, and raise feeders and drinkers so droppings don't fall in. Prompt treatment saves most birds.

instruction: I keep losing chickens to hawks and to predators at night. How do I stop this?
output: Provide a secure night house with solid walls, a lockable door, and small wire mesh over openings to block snakes, rats, mongoose, and wild cats, and shut the birds in every evening. Against hawks, give daytime cover such as bushes or a shaded run, and keep chicks near the hen or in a covered pen. A guard dog and clearing hiding spots also help.

instruction: How dry should my maize be before I store it?
output: Dry grain to about 13% moisture or lower before storage; damp grain rots and grows mould. Simple tests: dry maize is hard and cracks rather than bends when bitten, and salt shaken in a bottle with the grain will not stick to the sides. Dry on tarpaulins or raised racks in the sun, never on bare ground, and turn it often. Store only clean, fully dry, undamaged grain.

instruction: How can I store my grain without using chemicals?
output: Use hermetic (airtight) storage. Put well-dried grain into a tightly sealed metal drum, airtight container, or hermetic bag and close it fully. Insects inside soon use up the oxygen and die, and none can enter, so no pesticide is needed. Fill the container as full as possible and keep it sealed. The grain must be very dry first, or it will mould.

instruction: Weevils destroy my stored beans. How do I keep them safe?
output: Those are bruchids (bean weevils) that begin in the field. Dry the beans well, then store them airtight in a sealed bottle, drum, or hermetic bag so the pests suffocate. Coating the seed with a little cooking oil or wood ash stops egg-laying. Sun-heating or briefly freezing the beans before sealing kills eggs already present. Remove any infested beans first.

instruction: How do I store my potatoes so they last longer?
output: First cure them: keep tubers 1-2 weeks in a shaded, airy place so the skins toughen. Then store only sound, undamaged tubers in a cool, dark, well-ventilated spot on a raised slatted floor, not a sealed sack. Keep them out of light so they don't turn green, since green parts are toxic. Check often and remove any rotting tubers quickly.

instruction: How do I store sweet potatoes or cassava that I have harvested?
output: Sweet potatoes keep best in a cool, dry, well-ventilated shade on slatted shelves; don't wash them, and keep curing for a week after harvest, and cull any cut or bruised roots. Cassava can stay in the ground as a natural store, or be peeled, washed, and dried into dry chips in the sun. Cut cassava roots spoil within a few days, so dry or process them fast.

instruction: How do I know the rains are truly established before planting?
output: Don't rush in after the first shower. Wait for an effective onset: about 20mm or more of rainfall over a couple of days that wets the soil at least 20cm deep, then continued rains in the following weeks. Planting early can mean crop failure; planting too late shortens the season. Follow local advice and use a short-season variety if planting late.

instruction: We have a short rainy season. Which crops should I plant?
output: Choose fast-maturing crops and varieties that finish before the rains end. Good options are early beans (60-70 days), cowpeas, sweet potatoes, and short-season maize such as early-maturing or drought-tolerant hybrids. Plant as soon as the rains establish, use all available land, and interplant so one crop uses space while another matures quickly.

instruction: Should I plant before the rains come, in dry soil?
output: Generally no. Wait until the rains are established, because seed germinating in dry soil can rot or die during a dry spell, and weeds get a head start. Exceptions are crops like pearl millet and some groundnuts, which tolerate dry planting in some areas. When planting late, choose a fast-maturing variety rather than taking the risk.

instruction: The rains stopped early in the middle of my maize growing. What can I save?
output: Milk those stored soils: weed now, because weeds steal moisture, and loosen any crust so rain soaks in. Mulch around plants to hold soil moisture. If maize is already flowering, that's the critical time; any rain is gold. Prepare to switch to short-season crops or harvest early for fodder if the crop is beyond saving.

instruction: I live in a dry area with low and unreliable rain. What crops will survive?
output: Choose crops that thrive on little water: pearl millet, sorghum, cowpeas, pigeon peas, groundnuts, cassava, and sweet potatoes are proven choices. Plant local, well-adapted varieties, space plants a little wider to reduce moisture competition, and stagger planting dates. Avoid spreading too much land, and use intercropping such as millet with cowpea to spread the risk.

instruction: Should I plant the improved hybrid maize seed or save seed from my own crop?
output: Hybrid maize gives a higher, more uniform yield if you can afford good rainfall, fertilizer, and fresh seed each season. Save local varieties or landraces if rainfall is poor or you cannot buy seed, because they are hardier and you can keep replanting. Many farmers grow both: hybrids on the best land, local seed on riskier fields.

instruction: How does intercropping help me reduce risk on my small farm?
output: Growing two crops together spreads your risk: if one fails from drought or pests, the other may still yield. A legume like beans or cowpeas grown with maize also adds nitrogen to the soil, covers the ground to hold moisture, and gives you food and cash from the same plot. Match a tall crop with a short one, and don't crowd them so both get light.

instruction: Why should I rotate my crops instead of planting maize every year?
output: Planting the same crop yearly drains the same nutrients and builds up its pests and diseases in the soil. Rotate maize with a legume such as beans, groundnuts, or cowpeas, which add nitrogen and improve yields the next season. A simple plan is cereal one year, legume the next. Rotation cuts pests like stalk borer and striga weed and keeps soil healthier.

instruction: How can I water my vegetables using less water in the dry season?
output: Water in the early morning or evening so less is lost to the sun, and put it at the plant roots, not the leaves. Low-cost drip lines or a bucket-and-hose drip kit save the most. Mulch the soil with dry grass or leaves to hold moisture and block weeds. Make shallow basins around each plant so water soaks in instead of running off.

instruction: How can I harvest and store rainwater for my crops and animals?
output: Catch roof runoff from your house into a tank or lined drum through a gutter. In the field, dig shallow trenches along the contour, planting pits (zai pits), or half-moon bunds to trap runoff where crops grow. A small lined pond or earth dam can store water for animals and dry-spell irrigation. Cover stored water and keep it clean to reduce loss and mosquitoes.

instruction: Why does water pool and my crops still dry out? How do I help rain soak in?
output: Bare, crusted soil sheds water instead of absorbing it. Break the crust by light tilling, and dig planting pits or contour furrows across the slope to slow runoff so it soaks in. Add manure, compost, or mulch to open the soil and hold moisture. On slopes, plant grass strips or bunds along the contour to stop water and soil running off.

instruction: Ta yaya zan shuka masara don samun kyakkyawan girbi?
output: Ka shuka masara da tazara ta santimita 75 tsakanin layuka da santimita 25 tsakanin tsirrai, ka sa iri daya ko biyu a kowace rami. Wannan tazara na ba tsirrai damar samun isasshen haske, ruwa da abinci mai gina jiki, kuma yana sauqaqa noman ciyawa. Ka tabbata qasa tana da isasshen laima lokacin shuka.

instruction: Yaya zan magance kwaron soja da ke lalata masarata?
output: Ka duba gonarka akai-akai, musamman a tsakiyar tsiro inda kwaron soja ke boyewa. Ka tara ka kashe qwai da tsutsa da hannu idan gona qarama ce. Ka zuba yashi ko toka a tsakiyar tsiro, kuma ka yi amfani da magungunan da aka amince da su idan yawansu ya yi yawa. Shuka da wuri da jujjuya shuka na taimakawa rage lalacewa.

instruction: Wace irin taki zan yi amfani da ita a masara kuma nawa?
output: A lokacin shuka, ka sa taki mai dauke da sinadarin phosphorus kamar DAP domin qarfafa saiwa. Bayan mako uku zuwa hudu, ka sa takin da ke dauke da nitrogen kamar Urea ko CAN domin bunqasa ganye da girma. Ka bi gwargwadon da qasarka ke buqata, ka sa takin kusa da tsiro ba tare da taba gindinsa kai tsaye ba.

instruction: Me ya sa zan jujjuya masara da wake ko gyada a gona?
output: Wake da gyada suna qara sinadarin nitrogen a qasa ta hanyar qwayoyin da ke saiwoyinsu, wanda ke wadata qasa domin masara a shekara mai zuwa. Wannan jujjuyawa kuma na yanke zagayowar kwari da cututtukan da ke kai wa masara hari, tare da rage kashe kudi kan taki na sinadarai.

instruction: Ta yaya zan adana masara bayan girbi don kada ta lalace?
output: Ka bushe masara sosai har laimarta ta kai kashi 13 ko qasa da haka kafin adanawa. Ka yi amfani da buhunan PICS na zamani ko rumbu mai tsafta da bushewa. Ka ajiye a wuri mai bushewa da samun iska, ka riqa dubawa akai-akai domin hana kwari da fumfuna da ke haifar da guba ta aflatoxin.

instruction: Yaya zan kare kajina daga cutar Newcastle?
output: Cutar Newcastle na yaduwa da sauri kuma tana kashe kaji da yawa. Hanya mafi kyau ita ce yin allurar riga-kafi: ka yi wa kananan kaji allura tun suna qanana, ka maimaita kowane wata uku zuwa hudu. Ka ware kajin da suka kamu nan da nan, ka tsaftace gidansu, kada ka gauraya sababbin kaji da tsofaffi ba tare da ware su ba.

instruction: Yaya zan ciyar da shanun madara don su ba da madara mai yawa?
output: Ka ba shanu ingantaccen abinci mai gauraya na ciyawa mai kore, busasshiyar ciyawa da ragowar wake. Ka qara abinci mai qarfin makamashi da furotin musamman ga masu ba da madara. Ka tabbata suna samun isasshen ruwa mai tsafta kullum da gishiri da sinadarai. Ka yi musu allurar riga-kafi da magani kan qwarqwata da tsutsotsi akai-akai.

instruction: Yaushe ya kamata in shuka masara bisa lokacin damina?
output: Ka shuka masara a farkon damina, lokacin da qasa ta sami isasshen laima bayan ruwan sama na farko da ya tabbata. Shuka da wuri na ba tsiro damar amfani da dukan ruwan damina da rage illar fari a qarshe. Ka shirya gona da wuri kafin ruwa domin ka iya shuka nan da nan da damina ta fara.

instruction: Yaya zan shuka rogo tare da kauce wa cututtukansa?
output: Ka shuka bangarorin rogo masu qoshin lafiya na santimita 20 zuwa 25 daga tsirran da ba su da cuta. Ka yi amfani da irin da ke jure cutar mosaic da na ratsin launin ruwan qasa. Ka shuka a kan tuddai da tazara ta mita daya, ka noma ciyawa akai-akai, ka tumbuke ka qone tsirran da ke nuna alamun cuta don hana yaduwa.

instruction: Wace irin masara zan zaba a yankin da ba ya samun ruwa sosai?
output: Ka zabi irin masara mai saurin nunawa da jure fari, kamar wanda ke nunawa cikin kwana 90 zuwa 120. Ingantattun iri da aka samo daga amintattun wurare na ba da girbi mafi kyau fiye da irin gargajiya. Ka tuntubi jami'in noma na yankinka domin sanin irin da ya dace da yanayin ku.

instruction: Yaya zan hana kwarin da ke lalata hatsi a rumbu?
output: Ka bushe hatsi sosai kafin adanawa, ka tsaftace rumbu ka cire ragowar hatsin bara. Ka yi amfani da buhunan PICS masu hana iska, ko ka gauraya toka ko ganyen da ke korar kwari da hatsi. Ka riqa dubawa akai-akai, ka fitar da duk hatsin da kwari suka kama don kada su yadu zuwa sauran.

instruction: Ta yaya zan hana guba ta aflatoxin a hatsina?
output: Aflatoxin na fitowa ne daga fumfuna da ke girma a hatsi mai laima. Ka girba a kan lokaci, ka bushe hatsi da sauri har laima ta kai kashi 13, ka guji ajiye hatsi kai tsaye a qasa. Ka adana a wuri mai bushewa, tsafta da iska. Ka zubar da hatsin da ya rube ko ya canja launi, kada ka ciyar da dabbobi hatsin da ya lalace.

instruction: Yaya zan yi takin gargajiya (compost) don wadata qasar gona?
output: Ka tara ragowar tsirrai, ganye, kashin dabbobi da sharar girki. Ka jera su a matakai a rami ko tulli, ka sa laima kadan ka juya kowane mako biyu domin shigar iska. Bayan mako takwas zuwa goma sha biyu takin zai kammala, zai zama baqi mai qamshin qasa. Ka gauraya da qasa kafin shuka.

instruction: Ninapaswa kupanda mahindi kwa nafasi gani ili nipate mavuno mazuri?
output: Panda mahindi kwa nafasi ya sentimita 75 kati ya mistari na sentimita 25 kati ya mimea, ukiweka mbegu moja au mbili kwa shimo. Nafasi hii huruhusu mimea kupata mwanga, maji na virutubisho vya kutosha, na hurahisisha upaliliaji. Hakikisha udongo una unyevu wa kutosha wakati wa kupanda.

instruction: Nidhibiti vipi viwavijeshi wanaoshambulia mahindi yangu?
output: Kagua shamba mara kwa mara, hasa kilele cha mmea ambapo viwavijeshi hujificha. Okota na uue mayai na viwavi kwa mkono ikiwa shamba ni dogo. Weka mchanga au majivu kwenye kitovu cha mmea, na tumia dawa zilizoidhinishwa pale mashambulizi yanapozidi kiwango. Panda mapema na fanya mzunguko wa mazao ili kupunguza tatizo.

instruction: Nitumie mbolea gani na kwa kiasi gani kwa mahindi?
output: Wakati wa kupanda, weka mbolea yenye fosforasi kama DAP kusaidia mizizi. Baada ya wiki tatu hadi nne, weka mbolea ya kukuzia yenye naitrojeni kama CAN au Urea ili kuongeza ukuaji na majani mabichi. Fuata kipimo kinachohitajika na udongo wako, na weka mbolea karibu na mmea bila kugusa shina moja kwa moja.

instruction: Kwa nini nibadilishe mahindi na mikunde kama maharagwe shambani?
output: Mikunde kama maharagwe na soya huongeza naitrojeni kwenye udongo kupitia vinundu vya mizizi, hivyo kurutubisha udongo kwa ajili ya mahindi msimu unaofuata. Mzunguko huu pia huvunja mzunguko wa wadudu na magonjwa yanayoshambulia mahindi, na kupunguza matumizi ya mbolea za viwandani.

instruction: Nihifadhi vipi mahindi baada ya kuvuna ili yasiharibike?
output: Kausha mahindi vizuri hadi yafikie unyevu wa asilimia 13 au chini kabla ya kuhifadhi. Tumia magunia ya kisasa ya PICS au vihenge safi na vikavu. Weka mahindi mahali pakavu penye mzunguko mzuri wa hewa, na kagua mara kwa mara ili kuzuia wadudu waharibifu na ukungu unaozalisha sumu ya aflatoksini.

instruction: Nizuie vipi ugonjwa wa mdondo (Newcastle) kwa kuku wangu?
output: Ugonjwa wa mdondo huenea kwa haraka na kuua kuku wengi. Kinga bora ni chanjo: chanja vifaranga wakiwa na umri wa wiki moja, na urudie kila baada ya miezi mitatu. Tenga kuku wagonjwa mara moja, safisha banda, na usichanganye kuku wapya na wa zamani bila kuwatenga kwanza. Chanjo hupatikana katika kliniki za mifugo.

instruction: Nilishe vipi ng'ombe wa maziwa ili wazalishe maziwa mengi?
output: Wape ng'ombe malisho bora yenye mchanganyiko wa majani mabichi, nyasi kavu na mabaki ya mikunde. Ongeza chakula cha ziada chenye nishati na protini hasa kwa wanaokamuliwa. Hakikisha wanapata maji safi ya kutosha kila siku pamoja na madini kama chumvi ya mawe. Chanja na tibu dhidi ya kupe na minyoo mara kwa mara.

instruction: Nipande mahindi wakati gani kulingana na msimu wa mvua?
output: Panda mahindi mwanzoni mwa msimu wa mvua, udongo unapokuwa na unyevu wa kutosha baada ya mvua za kwanza za uhakika. Kupanda mapema huwezesha mmea kutumia mvua nzima na kupunguza athari za ukame mwishoni. Andaa shamba mapema kabla ya mvua ili uweze kupanda mara mvua zinapoanza.

instruction: Nipande vipi muhogo na kuepuka magonjwa yake?
output: Panda vipandikizi vyenye afya vya sentimita 20 hadi 25 kutoka kwa mimea isiyo na ugonjwa. Tumia aina zinazostahimili ugonjwa wa batobato (mosaic) na michirizi ya kahawia. Panda kwenye matuta kwa nafasi ya mita moja, palilia mara kwa mara, na ng'oa na uchome mimea yenye dalili za ugonjwa ili kuzuia kuenea.

instruction: Nichague aina gani ya mbegu za mahindi kwa eneo lenye mvua kidogo?
output: Chagua aina za mahindi zinazokomaa haraka na zinazostahimili ukame, kama zile zinazopevuka ndani ya siku 90 hadi 120. Mbegu zilizoboreshwa zinazopatikana kutoka vyanzo vinavyoaminika hutoa mavuno bora zaidi kuliko mbegu za asili. Uliza afisa ugani wa eneo lako kuhusu aina zinazofaa hali ya hewa yenu.

instruction: Nidhibiti vipi magugu ya kiduha (striga) yanayoshambulia mahindi?
output: Kiduha hunyonya virutubisho kutoka mizizi ya mahindi na kupunguza mavuno sana. Dhibiti kwa kupanda mikunde kwa mzunguko, kuongeza mbolea za asili na naitrojeni, na kung'oa magugu kabla hayajatoa mbegu. Kupanda aina zinazostahimili kiduha na kuchanganya na soya au maharagwe husaidia kupunguza tatizo.

instruction: Nizuie vipi sumu ya aflatoksini kwenye nafaka zangu?
output: Aflatoksini hutokana na ukungu unaokua kwenye nafaka zenye unyevu. Vuna kwa wakati, kausha nafaka haraka hadi unyevu wa asilimia 13, na epuka kuweka nafaka moja kwa moja ardhini. Hifadhi mahali pakavu, safi na penye hewa. Tupa nafaka zilizooza au zenye rangi isiyo ya kawaida, na usilishe mifugo nafaka zilizoharibika.

instruction: Nitengeneze vipi mboji ya kurutubisha udongo shambani?
output: Kusanya mabaki ya mimea, majani, samadi ya wanyama na taka za jikoni. Panga kwa tabaka kwenye shimo au chungu, weka unyevu kiasi na geuza kila baada ya wiki mbili ili kuruhusu hewa. Baada ya wiki nane hadi kumi na mbili mboji itakuwa tayari, ikiwa nyeusi na yenye harufu ya udongo. Changanya na udongo kabla ya kupanda.
